descriptionAr: About the Role OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across EMEA by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls. In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for EMEA account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure. You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region. This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking. In this role, you will: Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for EMEA account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes. Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies. Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers. Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines. Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders. Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution. Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information. Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls. Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support. Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools. You might thrive in this role if you have: 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment. Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes. Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability. Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams. Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills. Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales. Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls. A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity. descriptionAr: Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. On the data team, that means building the systems that make our data reliable, understandable, and usable by both humans and AI. We're looking for an analytics engineer or data engineer who wants to build the foundation for an AI-native data organization. You'll design core data models, pipelines, semantic layers, data quality systems, governance practices, and warehouse workflows that power the entire company: helping teams make strategic decisions, operate the business, and move faster with trusted data. You'll also make sure those systems are secure, privacy-aware, and legible to AI agents, data scientists, and the rest of the company. This role is for someone who can operate at the boundary of analytics engineering, data engineering, data governance, and internal product. You care about dimensional modeling, dbt standards, cost-aware warehouse design, access controls, privacy, and the details that make data trustworthy. You also believe AI should make the data stack faster, easier to maintain, and more accessible across the company without weakening security or governance. What You'll Do Build the core data foundation - design and maintain high-quality data models, marts, and pipelines that make analysis fast, reliable, and reusable. Manage the data warehouse - help own warehouse architecture, environments, permissions, performance, cost, data lifecycle, and operational hygiene so the platform scales cleanly. Make the warehouse AI-readable - own the documentation, semantic context, metadata, lineage, and retrieval patterns that AI systems depend on to understand and query Perplexity's data correctly. Own data modeling standards - define and champion dbt patterns, dimensional modeling practices, naming conventions, tests, and review processes. Lead data governance practices - define standards for access, ownership, lineage, documentation, retention, quality, and sensitive data handling across the analytical warehouse. Build with security and privacy in mind - partner with engineering, security, legal, and finance where needed to ensure data access, sharing, and AI-enabled workflows are appropriate and controlled. Automate data quality and maintenance - build AI-assisted workflows that detect issues, explain root causes, suggest fixes, generate tests, and reduce manual firefighting. Improve data team productivity - automate repetitive workflows, improve tooling, streamline development, and make it easier for data scientists and stakeholders to answer questions. Partner across the company - work closely with data scientists, engineering, product, finance, and GTM teams to translate analytical needs into durable data systems. Shape tooling decisions - evaluate build-versus-buy tradeoffs, manage vendor relationships when needed, and choose tools that scale with the team. What We're Looking For 6+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, data scientist, or closely related role. Deep SQL expertise - you can reason about correctness, performance, joins, grain, and edge cases in complex warehouse queries. Strong data modeling experience - you've worked hands-on with dbt (or a similar transformation framework) in production, and you understand dimensional modeling, data contracts, testing, and how analytical schemas should evolve. Pipeline ownership - you've built, maintained, debugged, and improved production data pipelines. Warehouse management experience - you've worked with warehouse administration, access patterns, permissions, performance tuning, cost management, or operational ownership. Governance mindset - you think clearly about data ownership, access controls, privacy, retention, lineage, auditability, and the risks of making data too easy to access. AI-native working style - you already use AI to speed up development, documentation, QA, exploration, and repetitive workflow automation. Stakeholder fluency - you know how to turn messy analytical requirements into trusted models, metrics, and reusable data assets. Autonomy and execution - you can take projects from ambiguous problem to production-quality system with minimal oversight. Operational judgment - you care about reliability, governance, security, cost, and long-term maintainability. Bonus Snowflake administration, optimization, cost management, or warehouse performance tuning. Experience with RBAC, PII handling, data classification, retention policies, audit workflows, or privacy/security reviews. Experience with Databricks or other modern data infrastructure. Experience building semantic layers, metrics layers, metadata systems, or data catalogs. Python experience for data tooling, automation, orchestration, or quality checks. Previous experience as an early analytics engineer or data engineer at a high-growth startup. Why This Role Own the foundation - your work will determine how fast and confidently the company can use data. Build for humans and AI - the next generation of data infrastructure needs to be understandable by agents as well as analysts. High leverage - better models, pipelines, and tools multiply every data scientist and every stakeholder who depends on data. Small team, broad scope - you'll have room to define standards, choose tools, and ship systems that become company-wide defaults.

descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. You will be responsible for the strategic design of systems across our high-performance global edge network and microservice clusters, providing cross-functional influence to ensure long-term stability and performance. In this leadership role, you will guide capacity planning and the development of next-generation features for Cloudflare Tunnel, Mesh and Zero Trust Network. Strategically influence and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, including security, network engineering, SRE, and product management, to design and scale technical solutions. Review work from your peers throughout all stages of the development lifecycle to ensure high-quality, maintainable code. Foster a culture of technical excellence through mentorship, proactive code reviews, and establishing engineering standards across the team to ensure high-quality, maintainable code. Debug issues in complex systems and contribute to the maintenance and improvement of operational health. Drive the long-term technical roadmap and identify opportunities for system-wide improvements, ensuring our architecture remains resilient as we scale. Work with a wide range of technologies and programming languages, including Go, Rust, and Typescript, as well as various databases (SQL and No-SQL), Docker, and Kubernetes. Role Requirements 5+ years of experience in backend software development with a focus on building  secure and highly available distributed systems. Strong programming skills in Go, Rust, C++, or a similar systems-level language. Knowledge of modern Unix/Linux development and runtime environments. descriptionAr: About Us At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale. With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world. Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater. About the team: We are a small but mighty team of three analytics engineers powering LangChain’s internal data infrastructure and analytics. We’re a full-stack team, meaning we work end-to-end across the data stack, from data ingestion to enabling self-serve agentic analytics. Learn more about what we’ve built so far here ! About the role: We are expanding our data team and looking for a analytics engineer to join us. We build products used by elite companies and over a million developers, and data plays a critical role in sharping our strategies and decision making. In this role you will help lay the foundation for business teams to diagnose issues, uncover opportunities, and drive success using data. If you enjoy building data infrastructure and empowering teams with actionable insights, this role is for you. *Location: SF, NYC, Boston, or Remote U.S. What you will do: Build scaleable dbt models and context that describe our business, powering a self-serve analytics experience Work with and expand on our foundational data stack — Fivetran, dbt, BigQuery, Hex Connect data from a variety of sources (Salesforce, Stripe, Metronome, Postgres, etc) into our BigQuery warehouse Build dashboards that track progress against company goals and KPIs Analyze product usage and operational data to surface insights around customer health, adoption, and revenue Develop and leverage a deep understanding of our business metrics to drive alignment and decision-making What you'll bring: 3+ years experience in a related role (analytics engineer, data engineer, or similar) Technical proficiency in BigQuery, dbt, Hex, Fivetran, Segment (or similar tools) Detail oriented, enjoys data spelunking, and can synthesize findings effectively Curiosity and a strong business sense to help anticipate needs and generate meaningful insights Start up DNA. You thrive in fast-paced and unstructured environments and are energized by finding out what matters most You are self-directed - you don’t wait for process or oversight to start making an impact Compensation & Benefits: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, meaningful equity, and benefits such as health and dental coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, and life insurance. Actual compensation will vary based on role, level, and location. For team members in the EU and UK, we provide locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. Annual salary range: $140,000-$180,000 Compensation Philosophy: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. Actual compensation and offerings will vary based on role, level, and location. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. Benefits Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role You'll lead GitLab's Dedicated Infrastructure team, combining hands-on technical leadership with team development. Working with the team's Product Manager, you'll balance delivery speed and quality, guide architecture decisions, and lead the team through incidents. You'll demonstrate ideas through proofs of concept, give team members meaningful feedback, and use data to make prioritization and risk decisions. What you’ll do Partner with the team's Product Manager to set clear priorities and deliver with quality and speed. Maintain at least 99.9% availability for Dedicated infrastructure, strengthen security, and automate operations to support more tenants at scale. Give your team clear direction and meaningful feedback, and build shared ownership of development and operations. Improve the platforms and tools your team owns so feature implementers can manage their services in production through self-service workflows. Recruit, onboard, and develop productive team members, supporting their growth and accountability. Lead by example with proofs of concept and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted approaches. Simplify processes and automate repetitive manual work. Model effective incident management, lead timely resolution and escalation, and document and teach best practices across GitLab. Use data to prioritize work, quantify impact, and manage risk and technical debt. Explain technical trade-offs to stakeholders to support their decisions. What you’ll bring A track record of building and owning large-scale distributed services, with the technical depth to evaluate architecture and guide technical strategy. Experience with fleet management, Terraform, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and automated provisioning at a scale of 20 or more clusters. Experience owning services with 99.99% availability service-level objectives (SLOs), and an understanding of the operational practices needed to sustain them. Experience using AI tools to improve team productivity, with lessons learned from both successes and missteps. Experience building and managing accountable, high-performing teams, including addressing underperformance and making difficult performance decisions when needed. The ability to lead complex projects to completion without relying on a dedicated Technical Program Manager. Experience leading distributed, remote teams effectively. About the team We build and operate the large-scale distributed infrastructure for GitLab Dedicated, our hosted software as a service (SaaS) platform. Our work centers on availability, security, fleet management, and automated provisioning across tenants. We also build self-service platforms and tools that enable feature implementers to own their services in production. At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. We collaborate asynchronously, with autonomy, accountability, and transparency guiding how we work. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. In this role, you will scale a high-performing team tasked with bringing the world’s most innovative AI companies onto Cloudflare's platform. To thrive, you must bring a founder mentality and deep familiarity with the VC ecosystem to capture high-growth startups at inception. You possess a sharp understanding of the dynamics of the hyperscaler market and the AI landscape, allowing you to position Cloudflare as the definitive infrastructure layer for modern workloads. Finally, you are highly familiar with PLG sales motions, knowing exactly how to identify high-potential, self-serve developer accounts and seamlessly transition them into enterprise expansions. Responsibilities: Own and exceed quarterly revenue targets, driving both high-velocity new logo acquisition and strategic account expansion within the AI and startup ecosystem. Recruit, coach, and develop a world-class sales team, instilling a high-tempo, execution-oriented culture tailored to technical buyers. Effectively articulate Cloudflare’s value proposition across our connectivity cloud, including Workers AI, R2 storage, network security, and developer platforms. Partner closely with Product, Growth, and Marketing to seamlessly convert self-serve developer usage into structured enterprise agreements. Act as a key executive sponsor for high-growth startups, founders, and VC partners, positioning Cloudflare as the foundational architecture for the next generation of tech. You might be a good fit if you have: 10+ years of experience in enterprise software sales with at least 3+ leading sales teams A proven track record of leading high-performing sales teams in the cloud infrastructure, SaaS, or developer platform space. A strong understanding of modern application architecture, serverless computing, and how AI startups utilize compute and data storage. Active connections within the tech startup and venture capital ecosystems, with an innate ability to spot and engage high-potential accounts early. Hands-on experience navigating hybrid sales models that blend product-led growth with top-down enterprise execution. A history of thriving in fast-paced, rapidly evolving markets where you can turn ambiguity into clear, actionable sales strategies   What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! As Sr. Analyst, Employee Lifecycle Data, you'll own and look after the employee data behind all of it. You'll keep our Workday data accurate and well structured, and you'll make sure it flows correctly into the systems that depend on it. This is a new role in its current scope. You'll own employee data changes from start to finish, manage the data structure that shapes our org, and set up reconciliation and error reporting across our integrations. We're looking for someone who gets the details right, finds the root cause when data breaks, and builds processes that scale as Ramp grows. We're moving to Workday on January 1, and we want this person on board before go-live so they can run our employee data changes from day one. descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building. About the Role Sentry’s AI capabilities span infrastructure, product features, design, and data ingestion. We’re hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to connect this work across teams, helping them make decisions, manage dependencies, and deliver a cohesive product experience. Our AI/ML team is building a modular platform for model routing, agent execution, and evaluations. Issues Platform owns customer-facing experiences such as issue details, activity feeds, and notifications. Product Design shapes how these experiences work together, while Ingest provides the underlying data pipeline. You’ll lead the program across these teams: clarifying ownership, sequencing work, managing integration risks, and coordinating release readiness. You’ll partner with team leads to connect their plans and resolve gaps between roadmaps. You’ll also improve how engineering changes reach teams across Engineering, Product, and Design, along with Documentation and Support. Your goal is a lightweight process giving partners the information and preparation time they need before changes reach customers. You’ll join an early TPM team and help shape how the function works at Sentry. Success means helping teams deliver together through technical judgment, clear communication, and practical coordination. This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office. What You’ll Do AI Delivery Connect roadmaps across AI/ML, Issues Platform, Product Design, and Ingest into a shared delivery plan. Sequence platform capabilities, product features, and design work so teams address dependencies before they delay a release. Help teams assign accountable owners, resolve open decisions, and communicate commitments. Partner with engineering and product owners to define release readiness, including evaluation results, staged rollouts, eligibility, and access requirements. Bring ingestion and reliability dependencies into roadmap discussions so teams understand the risks behind delivery commitments. Drive risk mitigation with clear owners, contingency plans, and timely escalation. Give teams and leadership an accurate view of progress, dependencies, decisions, and risks. Change Readiness Build a lightweight process for identifying changes affecting other teams, notifying partners, and confirming readiness before release. Include documentation and support preparation in delivery planning, starting with AI features. Establish concise updates showing what is changing, when, and who needs to act. Review communication and readiness gaps with the teams involved, then improve the process. Keep the effort proportional to the change and remove steps which don’t improve delivery. How You Work You help teams bring structure to complex programs with unclear ownership or no established process. You listen to different perspectives, make tradeoffs visible, and help teams resolve competing priorities. You engage with technical details and connect architectural decisions to delivery risks and product outcomes. You raise risks early, propose practical responses, and follow through. You adapt processes to teams’ needs and simplify them when the value is unclear. You respect team ownership while helping cross-team decisions reach resolution. Experience coordinating delivery across multiple engineering teams with separate roadmaps and leadership. Technical understanding to review design proposals, discuss architectural tradeoffs with engineers, and identify integration risks and downstream effects. A track record of managing dependencies, driving risk mitigation, and adapting plans as conditions change. Experience creating or improving processes which teams adopted and sustained. Clear written communication, including program updates, decision records, and escalations with explicit next steps. Experience building alignment across engineering, product, and design through sound judgment and follow-through. Relevant experience might come from technical program management, software engineering, or another role involving ownership of cross-team technical delivery. Preferred Experience Shipping AI/ML or LLM-backed features, including evaluations, quality checks, and staged rollouts. Partnering with product design to coordinate design and engineering work. Working with data pipelines, ingestion, or streaming infrastructure. Building developer tools or technical B2B products. Improving release communication across engineering, documentation, and support. Experience in every preferred area is not required. Team Principles Make work visible. Keep plans, ownership, decisions, and next steps clear and current. Raise risks early. Give teams time to respond before delivery is affected. Reduce friction. Build practices which help teams get work done. Respect ownership. Support informed decisions and help accountable owners resolve open questions. Keep partners informed. Communicate changes to scope, timing, and readiness before they affect others. The base salary range Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $150,000 to $240,000 USD. descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building. Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future. About the Role You’ll own AI-assisted coding within Sentry’s Platform Engineering organization, building the systems and workflows AI coding agents need to contribute reliably to our codebase. Your work will span engineering teams, with Developer Infrastructure as your home base. Your first focus will be making internal developer systems accessible to agents. Many workflows currently depend on human interaction through a UI. You’ll identify the most valuable gaps, expose those capabilities through APIs, and connect tools such as Claude Code to complete development workflows. From there, you’ll improve the quality of AI-generated pull requests and automate recurring engineering work, including dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and maintenance. You’ll build the context and execution environment agents need: relevant repository information, tools and permissions, state management, tests, logs, recovery mechanisms, and evaluations. You’ll partner with engineers across Sentry to understand where agents succeed, where they fail, and which changes improve the development process. This role combines technical direction with hands-on implementation, from choosing the problems to solve through building, measuring, and improving the solutions. This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office to work closely with Platform teams and engineering leadership. What You’ll Do Set priorities for AI-assisted development at Sentry, using engineer feedback and workflow data to identify where agents would provide the most value. Make internal developer systems accessible through APIs and build integrations enabling agents to complete workflows across those systems. Build context systems and agent execution tooling, including tool access, permissions, checkpoints, retries, and logging. Develop automated checks, evaluations, and feedback loops to improve the correctness, maintainability, and review readiness of AI-generated pull requests. Automate recurring work such as security dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and routine maintenance. Improve supporting developer workflows, including issue triage and CI/CD, where they limit agent effectiveness or create repetitive work for engineers. Lead changes across engineering teams, build agreement on priorities, and measure whether the tools reduce manual work and improve delivery. How You Work You’ve used AI coding agents on real development work and have informed views on their strengths, limitations, and failure modes. You bring structure to ambiguous problems, choose a practical starting point, and follow through on delivery. You move comfortably between infrastructure, backend systems, and developer tooling. You know when to build, integrate an existing tool, involve another team, or stop work with limited value. You combine data with direct feedback from engineers to assess whether a solution improves their work. You explain technical tradeoffs clearly and build alignment across teams and senior leadership. Qualifications 10+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on ownership of production systems. Experience building developer tools, infrastructure, or automation used by engineering teams, such as CI/CD systems, internal APIs, code review tooling, or agent workflows. Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, with an understanding of how context, tool access, and validation affect their output. Prior machine learning experience is not required. Strong software engineering and system design fundamentals, including experience building reliable integrations across systems. A track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives from problem definition through implementation and adoption. Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical decisions and recommendations to senior engineering leaders. Nice to Have Experience building agent harnesses, context systems, evaluations, or automated pull request workflows. Experience with code review tooling, static analysis, or automated testing. Experience measuring and improving developer experience or engineering productivity. Experience with large-scale distributed systems or monolith decomposition. Public contributions to developer tooling or AI-assisted development projects. The base salary range that Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $220,000 to $400,000 USD, plus an annual performance bonus of up to 15% of base salary. A successful candidate’s actual base salary (or hourly wage) amount will be determined by a variety of relevant factors including, without limitation, the candidate’s work location, education, work and other relevant experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Role We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to help translate our products, their value propositions, and our broader brand strategy into audience-specific, globally relevant marketing programs. You’ll shape how people discover, understand, adopt, and engage with our products across markets and stages of the customer journey. You’ll connect product narratives, audience insight, cultural context, and business goals into strategies that make advanced technology feel clear, useful, and human. This is a high-impact individual contributor role for a marketer who understands how product marketing, brand strategy, audience research, and international growth work together. You’ll develop segmentation frameworks, lifecycle and go-to-market programs, regional insights, and partnership opportunities; then work across product marketing, growth, creative, partnerships, analytics, and regional teams to bring them to life. Your work will connect launches, product education, customer engagement, and ongoing storytelling into a coherent journey from awareness to advocacy. To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance craft with decisiveness. In this role, you will: Translate complex product capabilities, use cases, and value propositions into clear, differentiated messaging that is relevant to distinct audiences without losing accuracy, nuance, or the product’s ambition. Develop audience segmentation frameworks based on customer needs, behaviors, use cases, regions, industries, and stages of the customer journey. Create audience-specific messaging and campaign strategies for groups such as creators, builders, professionals, students, consumers, and emerging-market users. Lead cross-functional marketing programs end to end for defined audiences or initiatives, with minimal oversight, setting priorities across awareness, acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and advocacy. Lead research efforts including customer interviews, surveys, social listening, competitive analysis, market trends, and behavioral data. Turn research and performance signals into actionable audience personas, messaging frameworks, briefs, campaign recommendations, and market insights. Identify cultural, regional, and language-specific opportunities across global markets, and help adapt global campaigns for local audiences while maintaining a consistent brand voice. Develop go-to-market plans for new campaigns, product features, audience programs, partnerships, and market expansions. Identify partnership opportunities with creators, developers, communities, platforms, industry groups, and other audience ecosystems. Align partners across product marketing, growth, CRM, creative, analytics, partnerships, and regional marketing; resolve tradeoffs and shape creative direction to deliver coordinated customer journeys. Measure campaign and audience performance, using data to improve messaging, segmentation, customer journeys, regional strategies, and future marketing investments. Build reusable campaign processes and playbooks, and coach peers and junior teammates to improve planning, creative collaboration, and execution. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 5–8 years of experience in product marketing, brand marketing, lifecycle marketing, growth marketing, audience strategy, partnerships, or related fields. Bring deep familiarity with AI products, foundation models, generative AI capabilities and limitations, and common user workflows; this is a critical qualification for the role. Have experience translating complex technology and technical product capabilities into clear, compelling, differentiated customer value propositions. Are a strategic thinker who can turn audience insight, cultural context, product strategy, and business goals into a compelling point of view and an actionable marketing system. Can move fluidly between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution: building the framework, writing the brief, launching the program, and reviewing results. Nice to Have: Experience working with creators, developers, communities, partnerships, or other distinct customer segments. Experience working across cultures, regions, or international markets. Experience with experimentation, performance measurement, social listening, and translating signals into strategic recommendations. Experience in consumer technology, emerging products, developer tools, enterprise products, or other fast-changing categories. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Total Rewards team plays a critical role in attracting, rewarding, and retaining world-class talent in support of our mission to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The team designs and delivers compensation and benefits programs that are competitive, equitable, innovative, and scalable, while balancing global strategy, local market dynamics, employee experience, and long-term sustainability. About the Role OpenAI is seeking an APAC Total Rewards Business Partner to lead and support compensation initiatives and provide regional benefits execution and operational support across the region as we continue to expand our global footprint. This role will serve as a key regional partner, helping translate OpenAI’s global Total Rewards strategy into programs and practices that reflect local market needs, regulatory requirements, and the evolving needs of our employees. In this role, you will partner closely with regional leadership, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, People Operations, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and external partners to design, implement, and manage compensation and benefits programs across APAC. You will operate as both a strategic advisor and hands-on practitioner, balancing global consistency with regional flexibility while maintaining a high bar for employee experience and operational excellence. This role is based in Singapore and we use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the Singapore office per week. In this role, you will: Regional Total Rewards Partnership: Serve as a trusted Total Rewards advisor across APAC, providing strategic and practical guidance on compensation, benefits, market practices, and complex employee matters as the region scales. Compensation Strategy & Design: Support the development and evolution of base pay structures, incentive programs, equity frameworks, and other compensation programs to ensure competitiveness, internal consistency, and alignment with OpenAI’s global compensation philosophy. Benefits Execution & Operations: Partner with the International Benefits Lead to support the implementation and ongoing operation of APAC benefits programmes, aligned with agreed priorities and programme designs. Provide regional support for benefits rollouts, vendor coordination, employee communications and operational issue resolution, and surface local insights to inform programme decisions. Market Benchmarking & Insights: Lead compensation and benefits benchmarking and market analysis across APAC, translating external market developments, regulatory changes, and regional practices into thoughtful recommendations. Offer Strategy & Pay Decisions: Partner with Recruiting and HRBPs on offer design, compensation decisions, and approvals, balancing market competitiveness, internal equity, global philosophy, and local market considerations. Program Management & Governance: Support the effective administration and governance of regional Total Rewards programs, ensuring strong controls, data integrity, regulatory compliance, and consistent application of policies and practices. descriptionAr: Perplexity is seeking a Director of Events to own our external events worldwide: the ones we host, the stages we speak on, and the ones we sponsor. You will set the strategy, run production, manage the budget, and build the team. If you have produced a flagship and a dinner in the same week, know what a good sponsorship deal looks like, and want to build an events function from the ground up, this role is for you. Responsibilities Own events. Hosted, speaking, sponsored. Strategy, budget, production, results. Set the calendar. Decide which events we run, which we speak at, and which we skip. Produce hosted events. Launches, dinners, summits, roadshows. Concept, programming, venue, vendors, run of show. Run the speaking program. Pick the stages. Prepare the speakers. Manage sponsorships. Negotiate terms, design our footprint, and account for the spend. Run field events with Sales. Get the right customers in the room. Make sure someone follows up. Be Perplexity. Our events should look and feel like our product. Work with Brand and Creative on every one. Lead the team. Equal parts IC and manager. Build the system. Playbooks, event tiers, intake, vendors, agencies, budgets. Measure. Attendance, coverage, pipeline, signups. Know which events worked and stop doing the ones that didn't. Be on site. For the events that matter, you are in the room. Qualifications 12+ years producing events, including large hosted events, sponsorships, and field programs, ideally in-house at a technology company. Has built or led an events team. Has owned large budgets, agency relationships, and vendor contracts. Has negotiated sponsorships and knows a bad deal when they see one. Has run an executive speaking program: selecting stages, preparing speakers, managing the day. Knows production: run of show, staging, AV, registration, staffing, security, permits. Drives measurement. Has built event attribution and tracked brand sentiment, and reports what each event returned. Can partner with Sales, Product, Comms, Brand, Finance, Legal, and executives. Power user of AI tools. Most of your work already runs through them, and you can show us how. Based in San Francisco or New York. Willing to travel internationally.

descriptionAr: About this Role 👋 Hi, I’m Kevin . I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional. You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem. The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company. Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers. Can you identify and hire talented people? We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others? Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work? Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization? Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI? AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy. These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members. Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today. Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company. As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well. Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment. Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well. You could be a strong fit if you: Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome. Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion. Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty. Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned

descriptionAr: Overview The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices. We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand. As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery. What You’ll Do Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology. Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness. Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems. Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions. Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team. Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice. Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well. Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers. What You Bring Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others. Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task. Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners. Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills. Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process. Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate. Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure. Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.

descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. About the Role The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support. We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution. Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements. In this role, you will: Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents. Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation. Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers. Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through. Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners. Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams. Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes. Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates. Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations. Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed. Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure. Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments. Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation. Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally. You might thrive in this role if you: Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues. Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations. Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses. Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis

descriptionAr: About This Role Hi, I’m Casey, Head Customer Success Management and Customer Education at Ashby. I’m thrilled to be hiring our first EMEA-based Recruiting Operations Consultant to support Strategic, Mid-Market, and Startup customers in the EMEA region. In this role, you’ll be part of the Customer Education team, blending 1:1 customer consulting, CSM enablement, and educational content creation to scale advanced recruiting operations expertise, strengthen CSM RecOps literacy, and help customers achieve measurable recruiting outcomes. You’ll also collaborate with Professional Services to scope and deliver paid consulting engagements (SOWs), helping shape and evolve offerings such as Process Optimization and Fractional RecOps — and, when needed, building reports or processes on behalf of customers to support their goals. Day-to-day, this looks like: Delivering high-impact consulting via RecOps Connects (complimentary 1:1 engagements) and paid engagements, focused on recruiting strategy, analytics interpretation, and operational best practices. Partnering with AEs, CSMs, and Professional Services to scope, sell, and deliver paid consulting engagements using the RecOps SOW framework. Translating 1:1 consulting insights into scalable education — Academy courses, guides, webinars, and segment-specific playbooks — that go beyond “how” to explain “why.” Contributing to advanced product education (e.g., interpreting Quality of Hire dashboards, building analytics strategies) and shaping our most sophisticated Customer Education offerings. Partnering closely with the Product Team to distill your observations into tangible feedback. Enabling CSMs on foundational RecOps strategies and tactics. You Could Be a Great Fit If You have hands-on experience with Ashby’s product and are excited by the power it offers Talent Acquisition teams. You love helping customers learn — supporting them as they grow into power users. You are an excellent communicator, skilled at clear and concise facilitation. You can navigate a range of stakeholders (e.g., Heads of Talent vs. recruiters) and help them align on shared goals. You’re comfortable working across a spectrum of complexity — from solving simple interview plan questions to building advanced Quality of Hire reporting strategies. You excel at holding stakeholders accountable, setting clear expectations, and facilitating alignment. You are proactive about defining boundaries — enabling CSMs to own foundational RecOps work so you can focus on high-leverage contributions. You are skilled at enabling others, whether in 1:1 sessions or group settings. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company. About the Role We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work. You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next. In this role, you will: Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners. Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI. Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear. Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works. Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers. Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation. Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own. Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement. Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. Translate goals into technical requirements, milestones, and delivery plans; influence implementation choices; identify systemic risks; resolve dependencies and disagreements; and carry commitments through completion. Use casework, incidents, threat information, and customer feedback to improve decisions and the program. As priorities change, recommend what to do next and explain the tradeoffs and effects on existing commitments. You might thrive in this role if you: Have independently assessed consequential third-party, supply-chain, or comparable security risks, and can apply that judgment to unfamiliar vendor technologies and operating models. Understand security principles and controls, including data protection, access management, application security, prevention, detection, and response. Can reason about architecture, identity, APIs, data flows, logging, integrations, and whether controls work. Know relevant frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and SOC 2, and can use them to inform an assessment of the actual engagement. Have translated security findings and requirements into practical contractual positions with Legal, Procurement, and vendor representatives. Have delivered useful products or workflow improvements, tested expected behavior and failure cases, learned from users, and owned performance after launch. Can use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test working solutions. Have independently delivered cross-functional programs, turned ambiguity into technical requirements and plans, and adapted priorities to achieve measurable outcomes. Can judge when to build, use existing systems, or engage partners to resolve blockers. Build constructive relationships with Security, Engineering, Product, Privacy, Legal, business teams, and vendors. Communicate complex security issues clearly in writing and conversation, including your recommendation, supporting evidence, and relevant tradeoffs. Question assumptions, try thoughtful new approaches, investigate unfamiliar systems, and revise your judgment when new evidence changes the situation. descriptionAr: ClickHouse is hiring an EMEA People Business Partner Lead to be the primary strategic People partner to business leaders across the region. By combining deep business partnership, organizational insight, and proactive People strategy, this role will help shape how the EMEA organization evolves—not simply respond to the needs of the business as they arise. This role is responsible for deeply understanding the business, its growth strategy, and the unique dynamics across EMEA, and translating that understanding into proactive People and organizational strategy. You will help leaders anticipate needs, spot risks and opportunities, and build the teams, leadership capability, and practices required to scale. In this role, you will help leaders anticipate organizational needs and identify risks and opportunities, while enabling them with the leadership capability and people practices needed to scale their teams successfully. Success in this role requires strong business acumen, organizational judgment, and the ability to move beyond responding to leadership requests to independently identifying what the business needs. Because EMEA is a diverse and complex region, this person must be able to understand the different business and market dynamics across countries while maintaining a cohesive view of the region and its long-term organizational needs. What You’ll Do Strategic People & Business Partnership Serve as the primary People partner to our managers and leaders based in EMEA, deeply understanding their growth strategy, operating model, and organizational dynamics. Translate business priorities into proactive People and organizational strategies, bringing an independent point of view and identifying risks and opportunities early. Partner with leaders on complex organizational decisions and ensure People is embedded early in business planning. Organizational Strategy & Effectiveness Partner with EMEA leadership on organizational design, workforce planning, role clarity, team effectiveness, and leadership capability. Identify patterns and systemic issues across teams and translate insights into recommendations and action. Use workforce, talent, and organizational data to inform performance, talent, succession, and organizational decisions. People Strategy & Program Leadership Partner with global People teams to adapt programs for regional needs and identify gaps or opportunities for improvement. Drive adoption and effectiveness of People initiatives, bringing regional insights back to the global People organization. Global Partnership & Influence Serve as the strategic People partner to leaders navigating complex employee and organizational situations across EMEA. Partner with People Operations and Legal to navigate performance, conduct, organizational change, and other complex people matters. Identify patterns and proactively address broader organizational or leadership issues. Bridge EMEA leadership and the global People organization, ensuring regional needs inform company-wide People strategy. Partner across People, Finance, Recruiting, Compensation, Legal, and other functions to align organizational and talent priorities with business needs. Influence across geographies and functions in a global, distributed environment. What We’re Looking For Significant experience in senior HR Business Partner or People leadership roles, ideally supporting complex, high-growth businesses across EMEA. Demonstrated ability to develop a deep understanding of a business and translate business strategy into proactive People and organizational strategy. Strong experience in organizational design, workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, talent strategy, and leadership partnership. Proven ability to influence senior business leaders and bring an independent, well-informed point of view to complex decisions. Demonstrated pattern recognition and judgment, with the ability to identify organizational risks and opportunities before they become visible problems. Experience developing or adapting People programs to meet business needs and driving adoption and measurable outcomes. Strong business acumen and curiosity, with a genuine interest in understanding how the business operates and what drives success.
